question: While learning to cook, Rajesh noticed that when he crushed a dozen of groundnuts in a grinder, it gets lined with oil. Whereas no oil is released when he grinds a bowl of cumin. What could be the reason behind this difference?

options.text: The fat in groundnut releases oil.
The protein in groundnut releases oil.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**The fat in groundnut releases oil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Groundnuts** are rich in **fat content**, specifically natural oils.
 
• When groundnuts are crushed in a grinder, the **mechanical pressure** causes the natural fats to release as oil.
 
• This oil lining can be observed on the walls of the grinder due to the **high oil concentration** in groundnuts.
 
• In contrast, **cumin seeds** have a significantly lower fat content, which is why no oil is released when they are ground.
 
• The difference lies in the **chemical composition** of groundnuts and cumin. Groundnuts are a source of edible oil, while cumin seeds are primarily used for their **aromatic compounds**.
 
• This phenomenon is a direct result of the **oil extraction process**, which is naturally triggered by grinding high-fat content foods like groundnuts.
 
• Understanding this difference is crucial in cooking and food processing, as it explains why some ingredients release oil when processed, while others do not.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cumin was of bad quality**__

 __
 
• The quality of cumin does not determine whether oil will be released during grinding. The absence of oil release is due to the **low fat content** in cumin, not its quality.
 
 
 
• **The protein in groundnut releases oil**__
 __
 
• Proteins do not release oil. Oils are derived from the **fat content**, not proteins, as proteins are primarily involved in structural and metabolic functions in food.
 
 
 
• **The groundnut was not dried**__
 
 
• Drying affects moisture levels but does not impact the **oil release** significantly. The release of oil is primarily due to the high fat content in groundnuts, not their drying state.
